## Clean Data

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(readxl)
library(scales)

# load the data, skipping the first two title rows
raw_bls <- read_excel("cu-income-quintiles-before-taxes-2024 (1).xlsx", skip = 2) 

# rename columns to be more code friendly
names(raw_bls) <- c("category", "all_units", "q1_lowest", "q2", "q3", "q4", "q5_highest")


# this creates a new column with the actual item name, and pulls it down to align with the mean data rows
clean_bls <- raw_bls |>
  mutate(
    # these are the main category headers 
    main_item = if_else(!category %in% c("Mean", "SE", "Share", "RSE", "Lower limit", NA), 
                        str_trim(category), 
                        NA_character_)
  ) |>
  fill(main_item, .direction = "down") |>
  # filter for average dollar amounts
  filter(category == "Mean") |>
  select(-category) |> 
  relocate(main_item)

# extracting specific data
expenditure_data <- clean_bls |>
  filter(main_item == "Average annual expenditures") |>
  pivot_longer(cols = q1_lowest:q5_highest, names_to = "quintile", values_to = "total_expenditures") |>
  mutate(total_expenditures = as.numeric(total_expenditures)) |>
  select(quintile, total_expenditures)

# isolate the two distinct necessity categories
target_necessities <- c("Food", "Housing")

```

```{r}
#| echo: false

necessities_data <- clean_bls |>
  filter(main_item %in% target_necessities) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = q1_lowest:q5_highest, names_to = "quintile", values_to = "amount") |>
  mutate(amount = as.numeric(amount))

# calculate percentages based on total expend
plot_data <- necessities_data |>
  left_join(expenditure_data, by = "quintile") |>
  mutate(percentage = amount / total_expenditures) |>
  select(quintile, main_item, percentage)

# calculate remaining equal to 100 percent
remainder_data <- plot_data |>
  group_by(quintile) |>
  summarize(total_necessity_pct = sum(percentage), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    main_item = "Other",
    percentage = 1 - total_necessity_pct
  ) |>
  select(quintile, main_item, percentage)

# combine and order the factors for stacking
final_df <- bind_rows(plot_data, remainder_data) |>
  mutate(quintile = factor(quintile, levels = c("q1_lowest", "q2", "q3", "q4", "q5_highest"))) |>
  mutate(main_item = factor(main_item, levels = c(
    "Other",
    "Food",
    "Housing"
  )))

# create a label for the top of the bars
label_df <- plot_data |>
  group_by(quintile) |>
  summarize(total_necessity_pct = sum(percentage), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(expenditure_data, by = "quintile") |>
  mutate(
    # two-line label
    combined_label = paste0(
      dollar(total_expenditures), 
      "\n(", 
      percent(total_necessity_pct, accuracy = 0.1), 
      " Necessities)"
    )
  )

```

```{r}
#| echo: false
ggplot(final_df, aes(x = quintile, y = percentage, fill = main_item)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack") +
  
  geom_text(
    data = label_df,
    aes(x = quintile, y = 1.02, label = combined_label, fill = NULL),
    vjust = 0, 
    fontface = "bold", 
    size = 2,
    lineheight = 0.9, # brings the two lines of text slightly closer together
    color = "#2c3e50"
  ) +
  
  # color Palette
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Other" = "#e6e6e6",               
      "Food" = "#e63946",                                
      "Housing" = "#1d3557"                              
    )
  ) +
  
  # the 25% upper expansion 
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = percent_format(), 
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.25)) 
  ) +
  
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("Lowest 20%", "Second 20%", "Third 20%", "Fourth 20%", "Highest 20%")) +
  
  labs(
    title = "The Cost of Survival: How Expenditures Shift by Income",
    subtitle = "Lower-income households dedicate a vastly larger share of their total spending to necessities.",
    x = "Income Bracket",
    y = "Percentage of Total Expenditures",
    fill = "Expenditure Category"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right", 
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()
  )

```
